result.topic_en: A problem on the refraction of a light ray at a spherical surface of radius r with refractive index n, finding the parameters of the refracted ray's line from those of the incident ray, with explicit formulas for special cases.
result.transcription:
Aufgabe.

Ein Lichtstral fällt auf eine Kugelfläche deren Halbmesser $=r$,
Brechungsverhältniß $n:1$ ist. Abscissen $x$ werden vom Centrum
gezählt. Vor der Brechung sind die Gleichungen der Lichtbahn
$y = \alpha + \mu x$
$z = \beta + \nu x$
nach der Brechung hingegen
$y = \alpha' + \mu' x$
$z' = \beta' + \nu' x$
Man soll $\alpha', \beta', \mu', \nu'$ aus $\alpha, \beta, \mu, \nu$ bestimmen.

Ist $\mu = 0, \nu = 0$ so trifft der gebrochne Stral die Axe in
$x = \frac{\sqrt{(nnrr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)} + \sqrt{(rr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)}}{nn-1}$
und man hat
$\alpha' = \alpha \times \frac{\sqrt{(nnrr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)} + \sqrt{(rr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)}}{\sqrt{(nnrr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)} + nn\sqrt{(rr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)}}$
$\mu' = -\frac{\alpha(nn-1)}{\sqrt{(nnrr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)} + nn\sqrt{(rr - \alpha\alpha - \beta\beta)}}$

Ist $\beta = 0\ \nu = 0$, so hat man,
$\sqrt{((1+\mu\mu)rr - \alpha\alpha)} = P$
$\sqrt{((1+\mu\mu)nnrr - \alpha\alpha)} = Q$
$nnP + Q + \alpha\mu(nn-1) = N$
} gesetzt
$\alpha' = \frac{\alpha(P+Q)}{N} = \alpha - \frac{\alpha(nn-1)(P+\alpha\mu)}{N}$
$\mu' = \mu - \frac{\alpha(1+\mu\mu)(nn-1)}{N}$
Macht man $\alpha = \lambda\sqrt{(1+\mu\mu)}$, $\alpha' = \lambda'\sqrt{(1+\mu'\mu')}$ so wird
$\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{n}$
$\mu' = \mu - \frac{\lambda(1+\mu\mu)(nn-1)}{nn\sqrt{(rr-\lambda\lambda)} + \sqrt{(nnrr - \lambda\lambda)} + (nn-1)\lambda\mu}$

methods.what: Axis intersection of a refracted ray when the incident ray is parallel to the axis
Intercept of the refracted ray for an incident ray parallel to the axis
Slope of the refracted ray for an incident ray parallel to the axis
Auxiliary quantities P, Q, N for a meridional (planar) ray
Refracted-ray intercept and slope for a meridional ray
Refracted-ray slope for a meridional ray
In terms of the perpendicular distance of the ray from the centre, refraction divides that distance by n (a form of Snell's law), giving the slope formula
Slope of the refracted ray in terms of the distance λ
